# 1 Samuel Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 131v–133r | **Source Image:** 1SA_002_page_001.jpg, 1SA_002_page_002.jpg, 1SA_002_page_003.jpg

---

**1** And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, for I rejoice in your salvation.

**2** There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you, and there is no rock like our God.

**3** Do not speak so very proudly; let not arrogance come from your mouth, for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him deeds are weighed.

**4** The bows of the mighty are shattered, but those who stumbled are girded with strength.

**5** Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, and those who were hungry hunger no more. The barren has borne seven, but she who has many children languishes.

**6** The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.

**7** The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and also exalts.

**8** He raises the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to seat them among princes and grant them a throne of honor. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD's, and he has set the world upon them.

**9** He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked shall be silenced in darkness, for not by strength shall anyone prevail.

**10** Those who oppose the LORD shall be shattered; against them he will thunder from heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.

**11** And Elkanah went home to Ramah. And the boy was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli the priest.

**12** Now the sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.

**13** And the custom of the priests with the people was this: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,

**14** and he would thrust it into the basin or kettle or cauldron or pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.

**15** Moreover, before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat for the priest to roast, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, only raw."

**16** And if the man said to him, "Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as you desire," then he would say, "No! You shall give it now, or I will take it by force."

**17** And the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.

**18** And Samuel was ministering before the LORD, a boy wearing a linen ephod.

**19** And his mother would make him a little robe and bring it up to him year by year when she came up with her husband for the yearly sacrifice.

**20** And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May the LORD give you offspring from this woman in place of the one she has lent to the LORD." Then they would go home.

**21** And the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.

**22** Now Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

**23** And he said to them, "Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all this people.

**24** No, my sons; it is not a good report that I hear spreading among the LORD's people.

**25** If a man sins against another man, God may intercede for him, but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?" But they would not listen to the voice of their father, for the LORD desired to put them to death.

**26** And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and also with men.

**27** And a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Did I not clearly reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, subject to the house of Pharaoh?

**28** And I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me. And I gave to the house of your father all the offerings by fire of the people of Israel.

**29** Why then do you scorn my sacrifice and my offering that I commanded for my dwelling, and honor your sons above me, fattening yourselves on the choicest of every offering of my people Israel?'

**30** Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: 'I indeed said that your house and the house of your father should walk before me forever.' But now the LORD declares: 'Far be it from me, for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

**31** Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father's house, so that there will not be an old man in your house.

**32** And you shall look upon the distress of my dwelling despite all the good that shall be done to Israel, and there shall not be an old man in your house forever.

**33** And the man of yours whom I do not cut off from my altar — it shall be to consume his eyes and to grieve his soul. And all the increase of your house shall die in the prime of life.

**34** And this shall be the sign to you that shall come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall both die.

**35** And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest who shall do according to what is in my heart and in my soul. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he shall walk before my anointed forever.

**36** And everyone who is left in your house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and shall say, "Please appoint me to one of the priestly offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread."'"

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the core structure and verse count (36 verses). The poetic register of Hannah's Song (vv. 1-10) was consistently recognized. Key theological terms — meshiho ("anointed," v. 10), beliyyaal ("worthlessness," v. 12), and the divine sovereignty clause (v. 25) — were handled faithfully by all three. SOPHIA's consensus follows LOGOS as the baseline with selective adoptions from EMET and PNEUMA where they improve clarity.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 1 — "horn" imagery
- **EMET:** "my-horn is-raised in-YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "my horn is exalted in the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "The LORD has lifted me high"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS. The horn metaphor is essential to the theology of this song (connecting to "horn of his anointed" in v. 10). PNEUMA's dynamic rendering loses this literary thread.

### Verse 3 — "God of knowledges"
- **EMET:** "a God of knowledges" (preserving Hebrew plural de'ot)
- **LOGOS:** "a God of knowledge"
- **PNEUMA:** "a God who knows everything"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS with singular "knowledge." EMET's plural is faithful but awkward in English. PNEUMA's paraphrase is too expansive.

### Verse 5 — "the hungry have ceased"
- **EMET:** "the hungry ones have ceased"
- **LOGOS:** "those who were hungry have ceased"
- **PNEUMA:** "those who were hungry hunger no more"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts PNEUMA's "hunger no more," which correctly unpacks the elliptical Hebrew (they have ceased being hungry). EMET and LOGOS leave the meaning unclear.

### Verse 9 — "feet" vs. "steps"
- **EMET:** "feet of His faithful ones"
- **LOGOS:** "feet of his faithful ones"
- **PNEUMA:** "steps of His faithful ones"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with "feet" (Hebrew raglei), which is the literal term.

### Verse 10 — "adversaries" vs. "those who contend/oppose"
- **EMET:** "His adversaries"
- **LOGOS:** "Those who contend with the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "Those who oppose the LORD"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "those who oppose the LORD" — clearer than EMET's compressed form and more natural than LOGOS's "contend with."

### Verse 20 — "lent" vs. "dedicated"
- **EMET:** "the loan which was lent to YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "the one she has lent to the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "the one she dedicated to the LORD"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS with "lent" (Hebrew sha'al), which preserves the wordplay on Samuel's name and the act of borrowing/lending in 1:28. PNEUMA's "dedicated" loses this connection.

### Verse 21 — "visited" vs. "was gracious to"
- **EMET:** "visited YHWH Hannah"
- **LOGOS:** "the LORD visited Hannah"
- **PNEUMA:** "the LORD was gracious to Hannah"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "attended to" — the Hebrew paqad means more than a social visit; it denotes divine intervention. "Attended to" (cf. Ruth 1:6 in SOPHIA) captures the purposeful action. PNEUMA's "was gracious" is interpretively accurate but departs from the Hebrew verb.

### Verse 31 — "arm" vs. "strength"
- **EMET:** "I will cut off your arm"
- **LOGOS:** "I will cut off your arm"
- **PNEUMA:** "I will cut short your strength"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "strength" here — the Hebrew zeroa (arm) is a metaphor for power, and since v. 31 is direct speech from God, "strength" communicates the meaning more clearly while retaining the force.

### Verse 33 — "die as men" vs. "die in the prime of life"
- **EMET:** "shall die as men"
- **LOGOS:** "shall die as men"
- **PNEUMA:** "will die in the prime of life"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts PNEUMA's "in the prime of life" — the Hebrew anashim metim is notoriously difficult, but the context (no one reaching old age, v. 31-32) supports this interpretation.

### Verse 35 — "in my soul" vs. "in My mind"
- **EMET:** "in my soul"
- **LOGOS:** "in my soul"
- **PNEUMA:** "in My mind"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with "in my soul" (Hebrew naphshi), maintaining consistency with the standard rendering.

— SOPHIA
